diagnosis: The lone decision-maker was able to satisfy checks C1, C2, C5, and C7 without the hidden information because the scenario's default values and thresholds allowed generic decisions to pass. Specifically, the 30-day no-co-lead and no-one-to-one agreement (PF1) fixed the interim duration to 4 weeks, the interim facilitator to Mira, and required separate check-ins for 2 weeks. Similarly, the policy's more-than-10-participant threshold (PF3) led to requiring documentation of a risk plan, which was easily satisfied. The model defaulted to reasonable values for agenda notice periods and interim staffing choices, allowing the lone decision-maker to pass these checks.

C1.why: The 30-day no-co-lead and no-one-to-one agreement changes joint co-leadership to prohibited, requires separate weekly check-ins, and fixes their duration at exactly four weeks.

C2.why: Mira's prior promise changes the interim staffing choice to Mira and fixes the temporary arrangement at exactly six weeks.

C5.why: The 30-day no-co-lead and no-one-to-one agreement changes joint co-leadership to prohibited, requires separate weekly check-ins, and fixes their duration at exactly four weeks.

C7.why: The policy's more-than-10-participant threshold combined with a conduct dispute changes the structure to require two facilitators and an explicitly documented risk plan.
